svg.text: One key block in v0, line by line
The block's 128 threads (4 warps) run these lines once per key block j: 64 keys of K and their 64 rows of V. Each panel takes one line.
Blue: thread 0 (lane 0 of warp 0) and its values. Inside the k loop the figure shows k = 1, head dims 16–31.

All 128 threads at once: 512 pieces × 16 bytes = 8 KB, the whole tile.
tKgK[None, None, None, j] picks key block j; g2s gives
each thread 4 pieces of it (the copy figure in idea 4
Its atom, CopyUniversalOp, is a plain copy, so each piece
makes two trips: a global load (LDG) into the thread's
The store waits for its load, a trip to global memory of
hundreds of cycles, and ④ then waits for every store.

svg.text: tSsQ is not made in the snippet: the setup line above
makes it once, before any key block. Printing its layout
from CuTe, as print_partition_shapes.py does, gives the
shape and strides shown. Shape and stride are known when
partition_A(sQ) lays the tiled MMA over the 64 × 64 Q
tile. Each mma.m16n8k16 instruction reads a 16 × 16 piece
of Q, so the tile splits into 4 × 4 pieces: 4 warps down
(the (4, 1, 1) of make_tiled_mma), 4 steps of 16 head dims
Thread 0 is in warp 0, so only the top row of pieces
concerns it, and in each piece it holds 8 values (blue).
The result, tSsQ, lists those values and nothing else.
Each top-level entry of ((2, 2, 2), 1, 4) is a mode: one
direction you can step through thread 0's values in. 5b

svg.text: k: picks one piece per step,
Strides are distances in sQ, in values. A row holds 64 values, so 8 rows down is 512; the next piece across starts 16 values later. A mode of size 1 never steps, so its stride is 0.
K gets the same treatment: tSsK = partition_B(sK) prints ((2, 2), 8, 4). Its mode 1 is 8, one piece per mma (panel 7); its mode 2 is also 4, the same 4 steps.
5c. Why k = 0, 1, 2, 3: one instruction covers only 16 head dims
A score is a dot product over all 64 head dims. The
tensor-core instruction is m16n8k16: 16 rows × 8 keys, and
only 16 head dims (the k16). The hardware fixes these
So each score is built in 4 parts, one per 16 dims. Step k
computes part k and adds it into acc_S (panel 8). Both k's
count head dims; neither is the key matrix K.
5d. range_constexpr: the 4 steps are written out when compiling
What gets compiled: the body 4 times, k a fixed number in each
cute.size(tSsQ, mode=[2]) is 4, the size of mode 2.
range_constexpr runs the loop in Python while compiling
and writes the body out 4 times, with no loop counter at
This matters because tSrQ and tSrK are registers, which
have no addresses: tSrQ[None, None, k] must name exact
registers when compiling. A k known only at run time would
push the arrays out to slow local memory.
Q: 8 values into registers, 2 per load

svg.text: tSsQ[None, None, 1] is thread 0's share of Q piece 1: rows
0 and 8, head dims 16, 17, 24, 25. That is 8 bf16 values,
autovec_copy uses plain shared-memory loads (LDS), each as
wide as the values allow. Only neighbouring pairs sit next
to each other in sQ, so one load moves 2 values, 4 bytes:
4 loads per k, 16 per key block.
Q never changes, yet the loop re-reads it for every key
block. Round 2 replaces these loads with ldmatrix.
K: 32 values into registers, and an 8-way bank conflict

svg.text: One of those loads, by all 32 lanes of warp 0 at once (mma 0, dims 16 + 2t, 17 + 2t)
tSsK[None, None, 1]: for each of the 8 mmas, one key (0,
values, again in pairs: 16 loads per k, 64 per key block.
Shared memory serves a warp's load from 32 banks, 4 bytes
wide. A row of K is 64 × 2 = 128 bytes, exactly one sweep
of the 32 banks, so a given head dim sits in the same bank
In one load, lanes 4g + t read key g, so 8 lanes need 8
different rows of the same bank: an 8-way bank conflict.
Q's loads in ⑥ have the same problem. Round 1's swizzle
8 tensor-core instructions per warp, added into acc_S

svg.text: cute.gemm(tiled_mma, acc_S, tSrQ[None, None, k], tSrK[None, None, k], acc_S)
K pieces 0–7 at k = 1 (Kᵀ: dims 16–31 × keys 0–63)
acc_S over the 4 steps: each step adds 16 more head dims to every score
All three are in registers now. cute.gemm takes step k's
pieces. For warp 0: Q piece 1 (rows 0–15, dims 16–31)
times each of the 8 K pieces, one mma.m16n8k16 (HMMA) per
piece, each adding into its 16 × 8 piece of acc_S.
Each mma runs on the whole warp. Thread 0 brings only its
blue values and holds 4 scores of each S piece: rows 0, 8
acc_S is both input and output, so the 4 steps add up: 32
HMMA per warp per key block, and after k = 3 every score
covers all 64 head dims. Warps 1–3 do rows 16–63 at the
The rest of the key block, in brief

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: # ... mask, online softmax with quad shuffles, P -> shared memory -> registers, O += P V
The comment stands for the rest of the key block. Counts
are per thread, per key block.
The softmax combines each row across its quad with 4 warp
shuffles (two per row max). P then makes a round trip
through shared memory to become the A operand of O += P V;
V is read transposed, one 2-byte value per load: the 128
16-bit loads in v0's count. Round 2 reads it with
